task_description: Write SQL to join three tables and aggregate by category, returning top 10 results
golden_output:
SELECT c.category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(o.amount) as avg_amount
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY c.category
ORDER BY count DESC
LIMIT 10;

task_description: Design a recursive CTE to compute hierarchical aggregations on a 10M-row table; optimize for performance
golden_output:
WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy AS (
  SELECT id, parent_id, name, 1 as level, amount
  FROM categories
  WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.id, c.parent_id, c.name, h.level + 1, c.amount
  FROM categories c
  INNER JOIN hierarchy h ON c.parent_id = h.id
  WHERE h.level < 10
)
SELECT id, parent_id, name, level, SUM(amount) as total
FROM hierarchy
GROUP BY id, parent_id, name, level
ORDER BY level, id;

task_description: Write a 3-sentence summary of the binary search algorithm
golden_output: Binary search is a fast algorithm that finds a target value in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search space in half. It starts by comparing the target to the middle element; if they match, the search is done. If the target is smaller or larger, the search continues in the corresponding half, eliminating half the remaining elements each iteration.

task_description: What is the time complexity of merge sort?
golden_output: The time complexity of merge sort is O(n log n) in all cases (best, average, and worst). This is because merge sort divides the array in half repeatedly (log n levels) and merges at each level (n operations).

task_description: Compare REST vs. GraphQL: when should you use each? What are the trade-offs?
golden_output: REST is simpler and better for CRUD operations with fixed schemas, while GraphQL allows clients to request exactly the data they need, reducing over-fetching. REST is cacheable at the HTTP level, but GraphQL requires application-level caching. GraphQL has a steeper learning curve but provides better developer experience for complex queries.
